headline: eBay's Q2 GMV grew 14% FX-neutral on a trading-card-led US surge; it beat estimates and raised full-year targets.
guidance_note: Raised FY26 outlook incl. Depop (FX-neutral GMV growth reported as 11.5-12.5% vs 7-7.5% prior); Q3 GMV $22.0-22.4bn, rev $3.07-3.12bn, EPS $1.36-1.42.
key_messages: GMV $22.4bn, +15% reported / +14% FX-neutral; FX added ~1 pt.
US GMV $11.69bn (+24%) vs international $10.71bn (+6%), so growth was concentrated in the US.
Active buyers 136M, +2% YoY (flat QoQ); US active buyers ~+6%, US enthusiast buyers +9%.
Focus-category GMV +26%, now >40% of GMV; trading cards led (NBA Finals, World Cup); bullion lift faded vs prior quarters.
Non-GAAP EPS $1.60 (+17%) vs GAAP $1.21; Depop's ~9M buyers join the count from Q3.

consumer.big_ticket: Enthusiast/collectibles spend strong (trading cards, coins, toys, memorabilia); gold/silver bullion a smaller tailwind than in Q4-Q1.

macro_read: Discretionary enthusiast spending in the US was robust in spring 2026, but buyer growth was only 2%, so this mostly shows deep-pocketed hobbyists spending more rather than broad consumer strength.
notes: FY GMV guidance range 11.5-12.5% comes from secondary coverage (Teleborsa summary) and includes Depop; not verified against the release.
Revenue consensus is implied from Zacks' 3.85% beat; 24/7 Wall St cited ~$3.02bn.
Stock reaction on Aug 6 not found; left null.
No Q2 management comments on tariffs/de minimis were found.
